verdict: OK to lend in Ahmedabad engineering & capital goods — pursue export-linked, order-book-backed OEMs and fabrication units; avoid EPC-heavy and pollution-notice units until structural safeguards are in place.
title: Ahmedabad Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Engineering and capital goods in Ahmedabad means fabrication, machining, castings, transmission structures and process equipment — units that convert steel, alloys and bought-out components into order-specific hardware.** Cash comes in on milestone-linked contracts, not retail sales, so the working-capital cycle is the business. Rating commentary is explicit that EPC players carry a longer cash conversion cycle than OEMs because execution periods stretch [11], and that a longer cycle directly raises the funding requirement [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check the receivable-and-inventory days against payables before you look at the P&L; if payables are the only thing holding the cycle down, ask how much of that is stretched supplier credit that will snap.**

## What has changed now
**The demand signal is genuinely strong: IIP for NIC 28 output is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date [D], and exports are +19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D].** Gujarat is pulling ahead of the country on collections — GST +11.9% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D]. **But the local news is thin and mixed: 19 Ahmedabad industrial units received closure notices for air pollution on 31-Oct-2026 [1], and the only other local item is a skilling centre for semiconductor and green manufacturing [2][3], which is a talent pipeline, not current order flow.** Peer results show the split clearly — Skipper posted its highest-ever Q2 revenue with PAT up 56% [6], DEE's order book crossed Rs 1,300 crore with revenue up 77% to Rs 286.7 crore [5], while Suzlon grew revenue 26% to Rs 4,869 crore but EBITDA stayed flat at Rs 720 crore and margin fell to 14.8% from 18.6% [7], and Pitti is expanding into a Hyderabad greenfield through FY2030 while margins strain [4]. **Volume is not margin; price the second separately.**

## Where to grow
**Pursue OEMs and component makers feeding power transmission, data-centre power, railways and oil-and-gas piping — the order books in [5] and [6] show where the money is actually converting.** Prefer borrowers with export exposure, since the +19.8% Apr-to-date export number [D] is the strongest single data point we have. **Avoid pure EPC contractors with long execution tails and thin payables support [11], and avoid any unit sitting under a pollution closure notice [1] until the compliance status is closed out in writing.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the cycle, not the balance sheet: milestone-linked drawing power, receivables-backed limits, and a bank-guarantee sub-limit sized to the bid pipeline, since guarantees are a standard bidding requirement in this trade [9].** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly order-book position with client names, and quarterly GST returns matched to sales. **If order book is growing but receivable days are rising faster, cut the limit rather than wait for the annual review.**

## Early warning signs
**Watch for margin compression on rising volume — the Suzlon pattern of 26% revenue growth with flat EBITDA [7] is the template.** Watch for capex announced ahead of confirmed orders, as with the phased Hyderabad build [4]. Watch for any pollution or compliance notice [1], and for payables stretching beyond normal trade terms [11]. **Any one of these on a monthly statement means stop fresh disbursement and re-underwrite.**
watch: Monthly receivable and inventory days vs payables
Receivable days rise while payables stretch -> freeze limit enhancement and re-check cash conversion
Monthly order book with named clients
Order book grows but conversion slips past milestone dates -> ask for revised execution schedule and client confirmation
Quarterly GST returns vs reported sales
GST turnover trails reported sales -> ask for reconciliation before next disbursement
Monthly bank guarantee and LC outstanding
Guarantee exposure exceeds sanctioned sub-limit -> require cash margin before issuing further guarantees
Any closure or show-cause notice -> stop fresh disbursement until written clearance
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Strong IIP and export data offset by thin local news and pollution closure notices.
